dicas.texto: Você está indo bem! Para comparar frações em uma reta numérica, o que acontece se dividirmos a segunda reta no mesmo número de partes que o denominador da fração que queremos testar?
Tente definir o denominador da Linha 2 como 12, já que a fração que estamos testando é 21/12. Isso criará divisões menores que facilitam a comparação.
Ao dividir a reta em 12 partes, cada unidade inteira terá 12 marcações. Onde o ponto 21/12 cairia nessa escala?
Como a fração é 21/12, conte 21 marcações a partir do zero na sua reta dividida em 12 partes. O ponto coincide com a marcação de 7/4 da primeira reta?

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; pergunta exibida "Are they the same? Correct the equal sign."; DUAS retas numéricas de 0 a 2, uma acima da outra: na Linha 1 a fração dada já está marcada pelo tutor; na Linha 2 o aluno digita em quantas partes iguais dividir (campo de denominador + confirmar) e marca o ponto da fração equivalente; à direita das retas, a igualdade entre as duas frações é mostrada em caixas: as da esquerda vêm preenchidas e, na da direita, o aluno digita o NUMERADOR (o denominador alvo já aparece); há também um seletor de comparação ("≟", "=", "≠") entre as duas frações; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (dividir a Linha 2, marcar o ponto, digitar o numerador, comparar, concluir).

campo numérico do denominador da Linha 2 sem rótulos + botão de confirmar

imagem/rótulo do sinal de comparação entre as frações

dicas.texto: Look at the point already marked on Line 1 and connect it to the fraction shown in the problem.
Read the numerator and denominator of the reference fraction, then identify the matching point on the line.
The denominator tells you the size of each equal part, while the numerator tells you how many parts to count from zero.
Starting at zero, count the equal fourths until you reach the tutor-marked point and submit the fraction represented there.
The denominator tells you how many equal parts make one whole on the number line.
Read the denominator of the target fraction, enter that number in the denominator field, and confirm it.
Use the denominator from 21/... rather than the denominator used for the reference fraction.
Enter the number of equal intervals named by the target denominator, then press the confirmation control.
A fraction on a number line shows how many equal parts are counted from zero.
Use the denominator to identify the size of each interval and the numerator to count the intervals from zero.
Count twenty-one equal twelfth intervals from zero, using the labels on Line 2 to check your position.
Starting at zero, move through the twelfth marks until you reach the location represented by twenty-one twelfths, then mark that point.
Equivalent fractions name the same quantity, so the numerator and denominator must be changed by the same factor.
Find the factor that changes the original denominator into the target denominator, then multiply the original numerator by that factor.
The denominator changes from 4 to 12, so determine how many times 4 fits into 12.
Multiply the numerator 7 by the factor that changes 4 into 12, and enter that product in R1_user.
Equivalent fractions have equal values even when their numerators and denominators look different.
Compare the marked points on Line 1 and Line 2 before choosing the comparison sign.
If the two marked points coincide, choose the sign used to show equality.
The points match, so select the comparison symbol that states that the two values are equal.
Before finishing, make sure the number-line marks and the fraction comparison agree.
Review the denominator, marked point, numerator, and comparison sign in the fixed interface.
Check that Line 2 uses the target partition and that the right-hand numerator matches the marked target fraction.
When every field and mark is complete, press the Done button to submit the verification.

misconceptions.description: Aluno conta as linhas verticais (marcas) incluindo o zero, resultando em um número a mais.
misconceptions.feedback: You counted marks instead of intervals. The number of equal spaces between zero and one is the denominator.

nodes.description: Mark the point on Line 2 that represents the target fraction.
nodes.instruction: Mark the point on Line 2 that represents the target fraction.

hints.message: A fraction on a number line shows how many equal parts are counted from zero.
Use the denominator to identify the size of each interval and the numerator to count the intervals from zero.
Count twenty-one equal twelfth intervals from zero, using the labels on Line 2 to check your position.
Starting at zero, move through the twelfth marks until you reach the location represented by twenty-one twelfths, then mark that point.

nodes.description: Enter the numerator that makes the fraction equivalent to 7/4 with denominator 12.
nodes.instruction: Enter the numerator that makes the fraction equivalent to 7/4 with denominator 12.

hints.message: Equivalent fractions name the same quantity, so the numerator and denominator must be changed by the same factor.
Find the factor that changes the original denominator into the target denominator, then multiply the original numerator by that factor.
The denominator changes from 4 to 12, so determine how many times 4 fits into 12.
Multiply the numerator 7 by the factor that changes 4 into 12, and enter that product in R1_user.

misconceptions.description: Aluno não altera o numerador, focando apenas na mudança do denominador.
misconceptions.feedback: You kept the original numerator while changing the denominator. To preserve equivalence, the numerator must be multiplied by the same factor as the denominator.

misconceptions.description: Aluno usa a diferença entre os denominadores como um valor de incremento aditivo para o numerador.
misconceptions.feedback: You added the denominator difference to the numerator. Equivalent fractions require multiplying both terms by the same factor.

nodes.description: Select the comparison sign showing that the two fractions represent the same point.
nodes.instruction: Select the comparison sign showing that the two fractions represent the same point.

hints.message: Equivalent fractions have equal values even when their numerators and denominators look different.
Compare the marked points on Line 1 and Line 2 before choosing the comparison sign.
If the two marked points coincide, choose the sign used to show equality.
The points match, so select the comparison symbol that states that the two values are equal.

nodes.description: Click Done to complete the equivalence verification.
nodes.instruction: Click Done to complete the equivalence verification.

hints.message: Before finishing, make sure the number-line marks and the fraction comparison agree.
Review the denominator, marked point, numerator, and comparison sign in the fixed interface.
Check that Line 2 uses the target partition and that the right-hand numerator matches the marked target fraction.
When every field and mark is complete, press the Done button to submit the verification.
